lessons.title: Taegeuk 1 (Il Jang)
lessons.summary: The foundational pattern in the World Taekwondo syllabus, symbolizing Keon (Heaven and Light)—the beginning of martial creation and all universal existence.

lessons.title: Taegeuk 2 (Ee Jang)
lessons.summary: Symbolizes Tae (Lake)—inner firmness with outward gentleness, joy, and focused composure. The lake is peaceful on the surface but retains massive potential energy beneath.

lessons.title: Taegeuk 3 (Sam Jang)
lessons.summary: Symbolizes Ri (Fire and Sun)—radiance, enthusiasm, and dynamic passion. Introduces knifehand strikes (Sonnal Mok-chigi) and rapid sequential combinations.

lessons.title: Taegeuk 4 (Sa Jang)
lessons.summary: Symbolizes Jin (Thunder)—great power and dignity in the face of danger. Introduces double knifehand blocks (Sonnal Momtong-makki), spearhand thrusts (Pyonsonkkeut Sewo-jireugi), and side kicks (Yop-chagi).

lessons.title: Taegeuk 5 (Oh Jang)
lessons.summary: Symbolizes Son (Wind)—gentle and yielding like a breeze, yet capable of terrifying gale-force destructive power. Introduces hammerfist strikes (Mejumeok), elbow strikes (Palkup Dollyo-chigi), and stomping transitions (Jitchikgi).

lessons.title: Taegeuk 6 (Yuk Jang)
lessons.summary: Symbolizes Gam (Water)—continuous, fluid, adaptable, and flowing around all obstacles. Introduces roundhouse kicks (Dollyo-chagi), palm middle blocks (Batangson Momtong-makki), and opening knifehand low blocks (Sonnal Arae-makki).

lessons.title: Taegeuk 7 (Chil Jang)
lessons.summary: Symbolizes Gan (Mountain)—ponderous grandeur and unshakeable steadfastness. Introduces Tiger stance (Beom-seogi), Crane stance (Hakdari-seogi), Scissors block (Kawi-makki), Knee strike (Mureup-chigi), and Covered fist (Bo-jumeok).

lessons.title: Taegeuk 8 (Pal Jang)
lessons.summary: The final and most complex Taegeuk pattern before Black Belt, representing Gon (Earth)—receptivity, source of life, and rebirth into the Yudanja Dan mastery ranks. Features jumping double kicks (Dubal-dangsang-chagi), single mountain blocks (Oesanteul-makki), and turning elbow combinations.

lessons.title: Koryo Poomsae
lessons.summary: The premier Black Belt form embodying the indomitable spirit and noble courage of the ancient Koryo Dynasty warriors who defended their nation against foreign invasions.

lessons.title: Keumgang Poomsae
lessons.summary: Named after Mount Keumgang and the Buddhist concept of the Diamond (Vajra)—representing impenetrable hardness, spiritual adamantine resolve, and towering majestic beauty.
